evidence: Word-by-word against SOURCE.txt. Replaced words: "Get clear on what it is you want to do during the induction. What do you want not to do today?" Draft: "Think about what you want to do. Are there things you don’t want to do today?" Differences: sentence 1 - "Get clear on" becomes "Think about" (a softer verb; the guide's own is "Choose"), "what it is you" becomes "what you", and "during the induction" is dropped; sentence 2 - the open question "What do you want not to do today?" becomes the yes/no question "Are there things you don’t want to do today?" ("want not to do" becomes "don't want to do", generic "things" added). So the draft says a little less than the words it replaces, and adds no claim, condition, person or number; who does what is unchanged (the reader plans). The meaning SOURCE.txt asks to keep (his published guide: "Choose the question or quality you want to explore, what you’re leaving alone today, and how much time you have") is carried by the paragraph as it would read: what you want to do (sentence 1), what you don't want to do today (sentence 2), and how long (the unchanged next sentence, "How long do you want to spend on this?"), with question-or-quality carried by the unchanged bracket ("You don't have to do this on a problem. You can do it on something you want to experience more of..."). I weighed the three 'less' points against 'no more, no less'. (1) Softer verb: it changes how firmly the reader is told to settle an aim, but the step is still asked for, "Decide to do it." comes two paragraphs later, and the plain verb sits in his casual register; I count it as tone. (2) "during the induction" is the one thing left out; it is not in the guide's meaning, and the section title ("Before you begin"), the line before ("Read this page ... when you're awake") and "this" in the next sentence anchor what the questions are about, so the scope is not lost; I do not count it as a lost point. (3) Wh-question to yes/no: both allow the answer 'none' and both ask the same thing (name what to leave out today); the exclusion step and its "today" are kept. the_change says Emulate's first two sentences of the paragraph (sample cn), with no put-back fix; the draft is those two sentences and its gloss (what you want to do, what you don't want to do today) fits. The ledger lines for T14 and T15 in ADMISSION.json say the draft 'puts back' a point Emulate dropped; I see no put-back in the draft and did not rely on that wording. CONTEXT.txt holds the two sentences once, as the start of the section's third paragraph, followed by his unchanged question, bracket and closing instruction, and they read right there. One cosmetic point: the apostrophe in don’t is curly while the rest of that paragraph uses straight ones. TELLS: I went through T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the draft in its context and find none PRESENT. Closest calls: T02 and T09 - instruction, question, question in a pre-session list is a run of short prompts, but it is the guide's own three items in its order, the replaced words had the same shape, and the swap adds no prompt; T12 - 'want to do' against 'don't want to do' is a matched pair, but it is the guide's own pair (what to explore, what to leave alone today) and was in the replaced words, so a naturally necessary contrast; T26 - 'want to do' recurs across the three prompts, but each asks a different thing (what, what not, how long) and the replaced words had the same parallel; T14 and C02 - the dropped 'during the induction' is covered above (not a protected point; the reference is recovered from context); T22 - the coaching idiom 'Get clear on' is replaced by plain 'Think about', so the change moves away from coach register; T15 - 'Think about' is plainer than 'Get clear on', not a rarer word swapped in; T10 - the bracket two sentences later ('You don't have to do this on a problem') is a permission pattern, but it is unchanged context and not part of this draft. LINTER: "B7 short landing at paragraph end" - accepted: the linter saw the draft alone; in the section the question is the second sentence of a paragraph that goes on for four more (a question, a two-sentence bracket and a closing instruction), so it is not a landing. "D9 follows the source order" - accepted: an in-place swap that keeps the guide's order (aim, what to leave alone, time); T13 and T09 answered above. "E36/E41 heavy second person" (12.5 'you' per 100 words = 2 in 16) - accepted: the replaced words also have 2 'you' (2 in 21, 9.5), so the change adds none and the rate rises only because the draft is shorter; they are the reader's own planning prompts, with no generic scenery (E36) and a plain, not reassuring, voice (E41).
